purpose: Developer review ledger for updating altitude fields in docs/data/cvfr-route-graph.json from CVFR PDF/chart imagery. This file is not loaded by the app.

directionConvention.oneWay: If true, exactly one of inboundAltitude/outboundAltitude is null; null is the disallowed direction, not an unknown altitude.
directionConvention.reversedLookup: If the app has a route leg TO -> FROM, use outboundAltitude as the new leg inbound value and inboundAltitude as the return value.
directionConvention.bidirectionalMarker: A yellow altitude tag with pointed ends on both sides, like the maintainer-provided 1200 screenshot, applies the same altitude in both directions when it is on the same green route.

reviewRules: Use docs/data/cvfr-route-graph.json nodes and docs/data/airfields.json as the coordinate source; do not duplicate coordinates in edge records.
Green-route candidates came from sampling chart pixels between known endpoints; keep detection.greenScore/maxGap/samples for triage, not as proof of altitude.
Candidate sign direction IN means the yellow arrow points from segment.from to segment.to; OUT means the reverse direction.
In dense terminal areas, prefer the continuous green route and printed route number over nearest-pixel distance to a yellow sign.
For very short connectors, use the altitude sign just before or after the endpoint only when it is on the same continuous green route.

Do not reject equal inbound/outbound values by default; some CVFR route markers publish the same altitude both directions, especially double-ended yellow tags, when the same-route crop or an independent airway table supports it.
Do not invent a reverse altitude for one-way paths; set oneWay=true and encode the disallowed direction as null.
Ignore yellow labels from crossing blue, magenta, airport, or nearby green branches even when they are closer to the blue review line.
Keep status=candidate unless the value has maintainer-provided evidence or a second independent chart/manual review.
Omit shortcut candidates that cross an intermediate reporting point or airfield; use the adjacent chart legs instead so one altitude pair never spans an altitude change.
Rows with source=cvfr-map airway adjacency were seeded to expose sibling legs in the editable chart; verify those values against the official CVFR chart before treating them as reviewed.
